items.text: Strictly generating functors
$S$ with a small generating family $C$ embeds in $\widehat C$.
$i\colon C\to E$ a functor (most important case: a full subcategory). For $X\in E$: $C/X$, the category of pairs $(Y,u\colon i(Y)\to X)$.
\text{(a)}\quad \varinjlim_{(Y,u)\in C/X}i(Y)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }X\qquad\text{for every } X\in E
\text{(b)}\quad E\to\widehat E\to\widehat C,\quad X\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(i(-),X)\ \ \text{is fully faithful}
(a) $\iff$ (b). If $i$ is fully faithful, equivalent to:
\text{(c)}\quad \forall X\ \ \exists\ \text{a strictly epimorphic family } i(Y_\alpha)\to X
(a) $\Rightarrow$ (c) clear. Converse (assume fibre products): cover $Y_\alpha\times_XY_\beta$ again by objects $Y^{\alpha\beta}_\lambda$ of $C$.
X=\varinjlim\big(Y^{\alpha\beta}_\lambda\rightrightarrows Y_\alpha,\,Y_\beta\big)
Then $i$ (or the full subcategory) is called strictly generating: every $X$ is a direct limit of objects of $C$. Smallness not required in the definition.
If $E$ has arbitrary direct limits, $i$ corresponds to $i_!\colon\widehat C\to E$, left adjoint of the functor of (b).
i_!\dashv i^*,\quad i^*\ \text{fully faithful}\iff E\ \text{is a localisation (quotient) of}\ \widehat C

For $E$ stable under direct limits, equivalent: (1) $E$ has a small strictly generating subcategory; (2) a strictly generating $C\to E$ with $C$ small; (3) a full embedding $E\hookrightarrow\widehat C$ with a left adjoint.
A weak analogue of topoi (the adjoint need not be left exact).
Examples: $\mathbf{Ens}^\circ$ (complete atomic Boolean algebras), $\mathbf{Ab}^\circ$ (compact abelian groups). Not algebraic substructures.
(Room) Compact spaces: ultrafilters as an operation? Is the point strictly generating? No: $\mathbf{Comp}\to\mathbf{Sets}$ is not fully faithful.
What next?
(a) structures defined by finite inverse limits or products; (b) topoi; (c) existence of the envelopes for small families of limits (a technical proof, written up).
Warning: the $\Delta$ stated the other day was wrong — categories and functors must match.
\text{limits required in } C\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{preserved by the functors of }\Delta;\quad\text{never impose existence without uniqueness}
Finite inverse limits
$D=(D',\varnothing)$, $D'$ not all small categories. Problems 1 and 2 are solved in terms of the big $\Delta$.
C\subset C^{\Delta}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(C,\mathbf{Sets})^\circ;\qquad \mathrm{Env}_{D}(C)=\text{full subcategory generated by } C \text{ under } D'\text{-limits (iterated)}
Problem 2 as before: stabilise the arrows, then fractions. $C\subset\mathrm{Env}$ is full (special to inverse limits only).
R_0\in\Delta_D \text{ representing the theory};\quad R=\Delta\text{-envelope of } R_0;\quad R=T(\mathbf{Sets})^{\circ}
An algebraic theory for $D$ = a pair $(S,\Sigma_0)$: $S$ accessible, $\Sigma_0\subset S$ a subcategory ($=R_0^\circ$), not just $S$.
S=\text{envelope of }\Sigma_0\ \text{for all direct limits, keeping those of type } D'
A larger subcategory still generates but is no longer the envelope. Two cases fully explicit: $D'$ finite diagrams; $D'$ products.
Case: finite inverse limits
Representing categories $R_0$: small, with finite inverse limits. Dually $\Sigma_0$ small with finite direct limits.
\Sigma_0=S_{\mathrm{fp}}=\{X\in S:\ \operatorname{Hom}(X,-)\ \text{commutes with filtering direct limits}\}
Objects of finite presentation. Groups, modules of finite presentation.
\mathbf{Ind}\,\Sigma_0\to S\ \ \text{fully faithful (finite presentation)},\ \ \text{essentially surjective}\iff\Sigma_0\ \text{strictly generating}
S=\mathbf{Ind}(S_{\mathrm{fp}}),\qquad R_0=(S_{\mathrm{fp}})^{\circ}
Theories definable by finite inverse limits $\leftrightarrow$ categories $S$ with direct limits and enough objects of finite presentation.
Finite presentation is $\aleph_0$-accessibility; stable under finite direct limits.
Compact separated spaces: the point is not strictly generating — the underlying-set functor is not fully faithful.
Generating vs strictly generating: groups
\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb Z,G)=G:\quad \mathbf{Gp}\to\mathbf{Sets}\ \ \text{faithful, not full}
C=\{\mathbb Z\}\ \text{with } \operatorname{End}=(\mathbb Z,\times):\quad \mathbf{Gp}\to(\text{sets with }\mathbb N\text{-action by } x\mapsto x^n)
Not fully faithful: on $\mathbb Z^2$ there are maps commuting with all $n$-th powers that are not homomorphisms.
Variants of « generating »
Strictly generating: $E\to\widehat C$ fully faithful. Generating by epimorphisms: faithful. Generating: conservative. Also conservative on monomorphisms / epimorphisms (SGA 4, I).
X'\hookrightarrow X \text{ mono, every } i(Y)\to X \text{ factors through } X'\ \Rightarrow\ X'=X
In a topos all variants coincide. Groups: free groups of finite type, or the standard $\mathbb Z^{\ast n}$ (Lazard's choice).
Morphisms of such theories
T\to T'\ \longleftrightarrow\ R'_0\to R_0\ \text{left exact}\ \longleftrightarrow\ \Sigma_0'\to\Sigma_0\ \text{right exact}
$S'=\mathbf{Ind}\,\Sigma'$, $S=\mathbf{Ind}\,\Sigma$: the functors $S'\to S$ commuting with direct limits and sending finitely presented objects to finitely presented ones.
Enveloping group of a finitely presented monoid is finitely presented.
Case: products
$D'$ = finite discrete diagrams (or of cardinality $\le\pi$, or arbitrary products). New feature: adding arrows never adds objects.
One base object $X$: the category of all $X^n$.
\operatorname{Hom}(X^n,X^m)=\operatorname{Hom}(X^n,X)^m

\text{envelope of the point}=\big(\mathbf{Ens}^{\circ}\big)\ \Rightarrow\ \text{finite products: } (\mathbf{Fin})^{\circ},\ \ |{\cdot}|\le\pi:\ (\mathbf{Ens}_{\le\pi})^{\circ},\ \ \text{all products: } \mathbf{Ens}^\circ
Objects indexed by $\mathbb N$; the $n$-th is the $n$-th power of the first.
H_n=\operatorname{Hom}(X^n,X)\quad(\text{« functions of } n \text{ variables »}),\qquad H_n\times H_m^{\,n}\to H_m\ \text{(substitution), associative}
Lazard's analyseur; this is Lawvere's algebraic theory (finite products, one base object).
Realisations in $\mathcal C$: product-preserving functors from this category to $\mathcal C$.
\text{base objects } I:\ \ R_0=\big((\mathbf{Fin})^{I}\big)^{\circ}\quad(\text{category generated by } I \text{ under products})
Which pairs $\Sigma_0\subset S$ occur? $\Sigma_0$ stable under finite sums, strictly generating — not enough.
Characterisation of the pairs
The data: the pair $(S,I)$, $I$ a set of base objects; $\Sigma_0$ generated by $I$ under sums.
$S$ with arbitrary limits, (a) equivalence relations effective (universally), (b) $I$ tests effective epimorphisms:
X\to Y\ \text{effective epi}\iff \forall i\in I:\ \operatorname{Hom}(i,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(i,Y)\ \text{surjective}
(c) $i\to\coprod_\alpha i_\alpha$ factors through a finite subsum (e.g. $i$ finitely presented).
Limit requirements can be weakened (only sums of copies of $i$); delicate.
U\colon S\to\mathbf{Sets}^{I},\ X\mapsto(\operatorname{Hom}(i,X))_{i\in I}\ \text{ has a left adjoint and is tripleable}
Tripleable: faithful (conservative) and carries effective epimorphisms to surjections.
